title: Retain and inspect private invocation diagnostics
description: Retain bounded allowlisted diagnostic events for the published observed invocation path and support read-only lookup by exact invocation identity. This diagnostic behavior remains separate from command semantics, authoritative records, and engineering evidence.
inputs: Declared observed invocation family, safe semantic outcome metadata, explicit diagnostic configuration and event timing.
Private owned logging root and an optional exact invocation lookup request.
outputs: Recorded, disabled, or degraded diagnostic state without changed semantic result.
Available matching supported events or bounded not-found, unavailable, corrupt-entry, or unsupported-event diagnostics.
behavior: Attempt the contract-defined start/completion events with closed schemas, families and severities; preserve valid event boundaries under admitted concurrency and interruption.
Project only allowlisted metadata; exclude payloads, raw arguments, secrets, environment and identity/path disclosures prohibited by the retained privacy contract.

Apply declared ownership, containment and restrictive-access checks; perform finite lock attempts and bounded rotation only on owned names, never steal unverifiable locks or repair unsafe permissions.
Keep logging failure/disablement from changing command behavior, repository bytes, recovery, semantic stdout or exit. Dedicated recording interfaces retain their existing boundary.

Inspect only the exact invocation across bounded retained files, ignore unsupported/corrupt lines through safe warnings without raw content, and never rerun a command or assert that absence means it never occurred.

failure_behavior.condition: Logging path, permissions, lock, clock, event size or I/O prevents valid recording.
failure_behavior.outcome: Degrade diagnostics with the bounded nonrecursive warning required by the declared configuration; preserve command semantics.

failure_behavior.condition: Lookup input is invalid, events are absent/expired, or retained lines are unavailable/corrupt/unsupported.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return the distinct safe lookup outcome and available matching events only; do not expose raw lines or create workflow authority.

sources.basis: Functional Analysis of the IR-008 system obligations confirms this distinct published command/record responsibility. The retained CLI/Record Format contract supplies exact public operations and limits; logical behavior is defined before Module allocation.

Assign MOD-010 as the proposed accountable primary responsibility after Functional Analysis. Current product source contracts retain detailed behavior authority; allocation is not runtime adoption or complete AR coverage.
